newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police report attack on bank.
newsitem.headline: German police report attack on bank.

text.p: Unidentified attackers detonated an explosive device at a branch of Dresdner Bank in western Germany early on Monday, police said.
No one was injured in the attack in the town of Hattingen but it caused substantial damage, a police spokesman said.
It was too early to say who was behind the attack, he added.

Trade unions sharply criticised the bank last week because its investment banking unit was helping to finance a hostile takeover bid for steel and engineering company Thyssen AG by smaller rival Fried. Krupp AG.
The takeover was expected to cost thousands of jobs in Germany's Ruhr Valley industrial heartland.
After a wave of public outrage, Krupp agreed to hold talks with Thyssen to see if it could increase cooperation as an alternative to the takeover.
But Krupp has vowed to relaunch its bid if the talks do not produce a satisfactory result.

Police said the attack in Hattingen, which is close to the city of Essen where Krupp has its headquarters, occurred at 4.16 a.m. (0316 GMT). The force of the explosion smashed windows in a neighbouring bank.
